title: Impact of Export Curbs on Supply of Key Food Items to Singapore and on Singapore's "30 by 30" Food Production Goal
what_it_is: Impact of Export Curbs on Supply of Key Food Items to Singapore and on Singapore's "30 by 30" Food Production Goal

sections.label: Poultry supply and food targets
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment about poultry production targets, Malaysia's chicken export ban, poultry imports and the 30 by 30 target.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment whether the Ministry will consider setting some local production targets for poultry and poultry products under the “30 by 30” food production target of SFA to enhance the resilience of Singapore’s supply of poultry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) what has been the impact on local businesses and consumers in relation to Malaysia's export ban on chicken; (b) how has the Ministry been engaging with the Malaysian government on the supply of poultry; and (c) how will the Ministry protect our local consumers from similar supply shocks involving other products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) between 2018 and 2021, what is the amount (in tonnes) of live and chilled poultry imported into Singapore from each country or territory; and (b) what are the constraints to expanding the number of approved countries for poultry imports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether there will be a review of the “30 by 30” target on self-sustainability in food production in view of the rising food security concerns; (b) whether there are plans to accelerate self-sustainability in food production; and (c) what is the long-term target on local food production and nutrition needs beyond the year 2030.

sections.label: Singapore food imports
sections.summary: Singapore imports more than 90% of its food.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Singapore imports more than 90% of our food.

sections.label: Malaysia chicken export ban
sections.summary: Chicken from Malaysia is 34% of total chicken imports and 99% of live and chilled imports, about 73,000 tonnes in 2021, with frozen chicken as an alternative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Specific to the chicken export ban, chicken from Malaysia accounts for 34% of our total chicken imports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: While this accounts for 99% of our live and chilled chicken imports, at about 73,000 tonnes in 2021, we have the alternative of frozen chicken available.

sections.label: Local food production buffer
sections.summary: Singapore intends to grow more food locally as a buffer, producing up to 30% of nutritional needs by 2030, up from less than 10% today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Second, we intend to grow more food locally to serve as a buffer in times of supply disruption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We are building the capability and capacity of our agri-food industry to produce up to 30% of our nutritional needs locally and sustainably by 2030, up from less than 10% today.

sections.label: Support package for rising prices
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced a $1.5 billion support package including a GSTV Cash Special Payment of up to $300 in August for lower-income individuals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Instead, to address households' concerns over rising prices, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong recently announced the $1.5 billion support package which includes a GSTV – Cash Special Payment  of up to $300 in August to support lower-income individuals.

sections.label: Alternate chicken sources during ban
sections.summary: During the ban, businesses using chicken from Malaysia could access chicken from alternate sources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: During the ban, our businesses using chicken from Malaysia were able to have access to chicken from alternate sources.

sections.label: Malaysia chicken export prohibition
sections.summary: SFA was officially notified by Malaysia's DVS on 31 May 2022 of an export prohibition of chicken effective 1 June 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Although the news of the export prohibition broke on 23 May 2022, SFA was officially notified by the Malaysian Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) on 31 May 2022 of Malaysia's export prohibition of chicken to Singapore that was effective from 1 June 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Because of climate change, the Russia-Ukraine conflict and disruptions in supply chains globally, we expect more disruptions to our food supply ahead of us.

sections.label: Offshore islands for poultry farming
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry would consider using offshore islands like Pulau Ubin for poultry or agriculture with ecotourism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider exploring the use of offshore islands such as Pulau Ubin for poultry or agricultural users with aspects of ecotourism, so as to enhance the resilience of Singapore's food supply.

sections.label: Increasing Singapore food production
sections.summary: The challenge is increasing food production from under 10% to 30% using almost the same land, requiring up to tenfold productivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We invite other stakeholders to also come onboard to give us their suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: But ultimately, the challenge ahead of us, Mr Deputy Speaker, is how we should increase our food production from the current figure of less than 10% to 30%, with less than 1% of our land almost at the same amount of land that we are using now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In many cases, we are looking at productivity to the multiple of 10 times of what we are doing now, in order to give us the bulk that we need.

sections.label: Stores remaining open
sections.summary: Most stores remained open, and those that closed briefly reopened when news came of kampong and black chicken importation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Which are the ones that have closed and for how long?

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, that is why I think we speak with some confidence that actually, the majority, by and large, of the stores have remained open.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: And if they have closed, they closed for short while and when the news about the importation of kampong chicken and black chicken came, they reopened quickly again.

sections.label: Accredited countries for importation
sections.summary: The Minister says countries are accredited for importation, and Malaysia has 99% of the live, chilled market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Gerald Giam and then Mr Alex Yam.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I note the Minister just said that food safety is paramount but that has not hindered our diversification efforts, so what has?

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: On the first question, actually, we do have countries that have been accredited for importation and as I mentioned Malaysia has 99% of the live, chilled market.

sections.label: Reviewing licensing conditions
sections.summary: Consumers may be reluctant to try unfamiliar products, so licensing conditions are evaluated, as done for eggs and considered for chicken.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: They may be reluctant to try new products because it is not familiar to the consumers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, from time to time, we have to evaluate the need for licensing conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We have done so for eggs and we will think about whether it is necessary for chicken as well.
